correctness.rationale: The entire 24-vertex graph is defined by exact integer coordinates; all 276 unordered distances and all middle-scale faces are exhaustively enumerated. Acyclicity of 126, 878 and 8681 vertex-toggle pairs is certified by topologically sorting each complete oriented Hasse diagram (648, 6696, 93480 cover arrows). The scale-four signed integral Morse boundary is explicitly computed as a six-by-three rank-one matrix with a unit entry and equal first two columns, and a zero third column. Because the resulting four-skeleton is 3-connected, the degree matrix classifies the five-cell attaching maps and yields wedge five S4 and wedge two S5. Independent full simplicial mod-two boundary reductions confirm ranks. At r=5 only 12 antipodal forbidden pairs remain; at r=6 all faces occur. No unproved extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The arXiv:2302.14388v1 opening theorem and the ensuing graph-metric arguments are restricted to Platonic solids; its second page explicitly names Archimedean solids as an extension direction. Lemma 2.2 already gives the penultimate threshold cross-polytope observation, which is credited and does not imply the middle-scale classification. The closest three published computational summaries concern a truncated cube, truncated tetrahedron or Euclidean cuboctahedron, each with a scientifically nonidentical object or metric. Multiple alias and implication searches found no directly covering classification. Residual risk of unindexed equivalence and of broader theorems in unavailable nearby packages remains.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent exact computation could be unindexed under Coxeter-group, Kendall-tau or permutation-metric terminology despite the actual alias searches.

value.rationale: Determining every homotopy type in a natural graph-metric filtration on a canonical 24-vertex Archimedean solid resolves all its six nonzero distance thresholds, including three nontrivial middle stages. The scale-four two-degree wedge is a substantive natural example beyond the cited unique-antipode/Platonic results, with an exact small integral attaching matrix; this is not merely a routine count of Euler characteristic, a reparametrization of a different metric, or a small gain over a published table.
